newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MALAYSIAN GRAIN PRICES STEADY IN QUIET TRADING.
newsitem.headline: MALAYSIAN GRAIN PRICES STEADY IN QUIET TRADING.

text.p: Grain prices in Malaysia were steady this week, helped by a weaker ringgit, but with few deals, traders said on Tuesday.
"There hasn't been much going on, the market's been quiet," said a trader with a commodities house in Kuala Lumpur.
On Tuesday, the ringgit fell to a 42-month low against the dollar at 2.7930 in early trading before recovering to 2.7645 at 1000 GMT.
"Technically speaking, the prices should have come down this week but they have been quoted up because the ringgit has gone down further," said a dealer.
Dealers said there were ample stocks in the market, except for soymeal which was slightly short after some short-covering.
For corn, dealers estimated there were about 70,000 tonnes in Malaysia's central region this week, compared to the 80,000 to 100,000 a week ago.
Traders said bulk corn of Chinese origin in Malaysia's central region was quoted unchanged at 365-370 ringgit a tonne C and F this week.
Bulk Argentine maize, ex-factories/godowns in the central region, was also steady at 370-375 ringgit.
Wheat and soymeal prices remained the same, with thin volumes seen in the trading of both.
"A" grade wheat in Malaysia was at 650 ringgit a bag, while "B" grade wheat was at 430 ringgit.
Local soymeal was at 865 ringgit while imported soymeal was at 845 ringgit.
